title: Pride and Prejudice
author: d'après Jane Austen
desc: Elizabeth déteste le fier Mr. Darcy. Mais les premières impressions sont parfois fausses.

p: In a small village in England, there lived the Bennet family: Mr. and Mrs. Bennet and their five daughters. Mrs. Bennet had only one goal in life: to find rich husbands for her girls.
One day, she heard great news. A rich young man, Mr. Bingley, had rented the big house near the village, Netherfield Park.
At the village ball, Mr. Bingley danced twice with Jane, the oldest and most beautiful Bennet sister. Everybody could see that he liked her.
Mr. Bingley's friend, Mr. Darcy, was even richer. He was tall and handsome, but he didn't smile and danced with nobody. Bingley asked him to dance with Elizabeth, the second sister.
"She is not pretty enough to tempt me," said Darcy.
Elizabeth heard him. She laughed and told the story to all her friends. But inside, she was hurt. "What a proud, horrible man," she thought.

Some weeks later, the Bennets met Mr. Wickham, a charming young officer. He told Elizabeth a sad story: "Mr. Darcy's father loved me like a son. But Darcy was jealous. He stole the money his father left me."
Elizabeth believed him. Now she hated Darcy even more.
Then, suddenly, Mr. Bingley left for London, without saying goodbye to Jane. Jane was heartbroken. Later, Elizabeth learned that Darcy had told Bingley to forget Jane.
In the spring, Elizabeth visited a friend in Kent. Darcy was there too. One day, he came to see her, very nervous.
"I have tried to fight it, but I cannot," he said. "I admire you and I love you. Please marry me."
Elizabeth was shocked. "You destroyed my sister's happiness. You ruined Mr. Wickham. You are the last man in the world I would marry!"
The next morning, Darcy gave Elizabeth a letter. Then he left.

In the letter, he explained everything. About Jane: he believed she didn't really love Bingley, because she was always so calm. About Wickham: it was all lies. Wickham had taken the money and spent it all on gambling. And then he tried to run away with Darcy's fifteen-year-old sister, Georgiana, to get her fortune.
Elizabeth read the letter again and again. Her face became red.
"How blind I was!" she thought. "I was proud of my intelligence. But I believed the first charming man who flattered me, and I judged Darcy on one sentence. I never knew myself until this moment."
In the summer, Elizabeth visited Darcy's beautiful house, Pemberley, with her aunt and uncle. She thought Darcy was away. But he came home early.
He was completely different. He was kind and polite to her uncle and aunt. His servants said he was the best master in the world.
Then terrible news arrived: Elizabeth's youngest sister, Lydia, had run away with Wickham! The whole family was in shame.
Some days later, Lydia came home, married to Wickham. Elizabeth discovered that it was Darcy who found them and paid Wickham's debts so he would marry Lydia. He did it secretly, for Elizabeth.
Soon, Bingley came back and asked Jane to marry him. And one morning, Darcy walked with Elizabeth in the fields.
"My feelings have not changed," he said. "But one word from you will silence me forever."
"My feelings," said Elizabeth, smiling, "are completely different now."
Pride had kept them apart. Prejudice had made them blind. But love had taught them both to see clearly.
